Chapter 7: Discernment—Making Wise Choices Together.
Let’s talk about discernment. It’s that quiet, ongoing process of figuring out if you’re meant to move forward together toward marriage. And honestly, it’s never just a single big moment—it’s more like a series of thoughtful steps, each one shaped by prayer, reflection, and honest conversations.
Discernment’s all about using both your head and your heart. You’re asking practical questions, like—are our values in sync? Do our life goals actually fit together? But at the same time, you’re listening to your intuition, and looking for that sense of spiritual peace. Think of it as putting together a puzzle—each bit of information, each experience you share, helps reveal a little more of the bigger picture.
So, what are some gentle tools you can use for discernment?
First, there’s shared reflection. Take time to talk about what you’re learning—not just about each other, but about the relationship itself.
Then, seek counsel. Trusted mentors or family members can offer their perspective and advice, and sometimes they’ll notice things you might miss.
Don’t forget about personal prayer. Spend time alone, asking for wisdom and clarity about your next steps.
And, of course, test your compatibility. See how you handle differences, make decisions together, and work through conflict. These moments can teach you a lot about your ability to grow as a team.
Now, discernment isn’t about finding a perfect person or a flawless relationship. Every couple will face challenges and differences—it’s just part of the journey. The real goal is to honestly assess whether you can grow together, support each other’s faith, and build a life that honors God.
In practice, discernment might mean stepping back for a bit to get some clarity, or slowing things down so you’ve got space to reflect. It could also look like talking through practical issues—money, family expectations, future plans—just to make sure there aren’t any hidden surprises waiting down the road.
And yes, this whole process can feel heavy at times. But here’s the thing—it’s also incredibly freeing. When you make decisions with real intention and care, you can move forward with confidence, knowing you’ve done your best to seek God’s will and each other’s good.
